## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: will US forces strike inside Iranian territory between 00:00 UTC Oct 15 and 23:59 UTC Oct 16, 2026? (compiled 2026-10-05)

Everything below happened before the question window opens (Oct 15 00:00 UTC). It is background only and does not count toward resolution.

**Sourcing caveats**
- centcom.mil, metaculus.com, globalsecurity.org, thehill.com and washingtontimes.com refused page fetches. Anything from those sites comes from search snippets and is marked "snippet".
- Some CNN, CNBC, Axios and NPR pages were also unreadable, so a few dates rest on snippets.

## 1. Resolution source: what it says now

**Metaculus definition of "credible source"** (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions; snippet, not checked against the live page):
> "an online or print published article from a journalistic or academic source, information publicly posted by an authoritative source with specific knowledge or responsibility for the subject matter … provided … that there is no significant controversy surrounding its correctness. Credible sources will generally not include unsourced information found in blogs, social media postings, or websites of individuals."

**Last confirmed US strike on Iranian land or islands: Sep 1, 2026**
- CENTCOM release "CENTCOM Completes Strikes on IRGC Targets in Iran" (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/Article/4588389/; snippet). It describes "a wave of strikes against Iranian military targets... air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites."
- Targets were Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Sirik, Jask, Asaluyeh and Ahvaz, with about 11 killed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_2026_United_States_strikes_on_Iran
- Before that, on Aug 30, the US hit IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island. Al Jazeera called it "the first known military action from both sides since late July": https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/30/us-strikes-irans-lark-island-in-first-attack-in-weeks

**US strikes on IRGC-linked tankers**
- **Sep 5** (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/Article/4591744/): three tankers destroyed after Iran targeted two US Navy warships.
  - One "off the coast of Kharg Island", one "near Jask", and one in the Gulf of Oman.
  - Adm. Brad Cooper: "If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours."
- **Sep 8–9** (Al Jazeera, Sep 9: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/9/us-destroys-five-iranian-tankers-iran-retaliates-with-attacks-on-jordan-base): five more tankers struck. One, "M/T Derya", was "near Kharg island"; the rest were in the Gulf of Oman.
- **Uncertain:** whether the tankers near Kharg and Jask were inside Iran's 12 nm territorial waters. Similar strikes would count only if they are.
- **Unconfirmed:** an Axios headline dated Sep 2 about tanker strikes. It may be the Sep 5 event.

**Nothing found since about Sep 10**
- No CENTCOM or DoD strike release found for Sep 10 through Oct 5.
- GlobalSecurity's "Day 218" update (Oct 3; snippet, https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/ops/iran-war-oprep.htm): "no American or coalition strike on Iranian territory ashore was reported… a twenty-sixth consecutive operational period."
- criticalthreats.org (Sep 10) reported Iranian attacks (including a cluster warhead on a US base in Jordan on Sep 9) but no US strikes Sep 8–10.

## 2. Recent news, status quo and scheduled events (all dates 2026)

**Current state**
- The war began Feb 28 and is formally still on.
- There is no signed ceasefire. In practice the US has paused strikes since about Sep 10, while the US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.

**Diplomacy**
- **About Sep 26–28:** Trump rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire and Hormuz reopening proposal ("not acceptable").
  - CNBC, Sep 26: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/26/trump-rejects-irans-conditional-ceasefire-proposal-wsj-reports.html
  - NPR, Sep 28: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5982720/trump-rejects-irans-latest-ceasefire-proposal
- WSJ, via The Hill: Trump "has told aides he views renewed U.S. bombing after the midterm elections as likely": https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6113000-trump-iran-proposal-ceasefire/
- **Sep 30 – Oct 1:** Iran said it received the US response through Doha. Qatari (and Pakistani) mediation continues: https://www.business-standard.com/amp/world-news/iran-says-it-got-us-response-on-ceasefire-proposal-as-washington-exits-iraq-126093000961_1.html
- **Oct 1:** Time interview. Trump said it is "possible" bombing increases after the Nov 3 midterms, and "They'll either sign a very fair deal, or they won't exist any longer."
  - https://time.com/article/2026/10/01/donald-trump-2026-interview
  - https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/oct/1/trump-weighs-strikes-iran-midterms-britain-makes-arrest-suspected/
- **Oct 1:** criticalthreats.org says Iran's threats aim to deter the US from "resuming military action" after the midterms: https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/iran-update-october-1-2026
- **Oct 4:** Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until Iran's seven conditions are met, and that Iran will "both fight and negotiate." FM Araghchi said Iran is ready to defend itself: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/4/iran-says-strait-of-hormuz-to-remain-closed-until-us-meets-conditions

**Strait of Hormuz** (mostly snippets)
- Effectively closed; one transit was logged on Sep 27, against about 85 a day normally.
- Sep 28: a ship was hit by a projectile and caught fire.
- Unconfirmed: about 6 vessels hit in the week to Oct 3.
- Oct 2: a tanker was hit off Oman. Brent was about $102, and the G7 agreed to release up to 100M barrels.

**US force posture**
- Sep 27: the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group plus an amphibious group of about 2,000 Marines left San Diego.
- It is expected in the region around mid-November, which would make three carriers there: https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/oct/03/pressure-builds-on-iran-as-trump-boosts-us-militar/

**Scheduled events**
- None confirmed for Oct 15–16: no talks date, deadline or ultimatum found.
- IAEA Board and UN Security Council calendars were not checked.
- The key signalled marker is Nov 3 (midterms).

**Not researched:** Israeli actions since August.

**Triggers seen so far**
- US strikes have followed Iranian attacks on US ships or bases within 0–3 days. Examples:
  - The Aug 30 strike, followed by Iranian retaliation on bases in Jordan.
  - The Sep 5 tanker strikes, which followed Iran targeting two US warships.

## 4. Base rates

**Before 2026**
- Only about 1–3 days with US strikes on Iranian territory, depending on whether offshore platforms count:
  - Oct 19, 1987 (Nimble Archer): offshore oil platforms.
  - Apr 18, 1988 (Praying Mantis): offshore oil platforms and Iranian navy ships.
  - Jun 22, 2025 (Midnight Hammer): Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan.
- The two 1980s items come from the agent's background knowledge, not checked this session.

**2026 war**
- **Feb 28 – Apr 7:** near-daily strikes (about 39 days).
- **Apr 8 – Jul 7, during the "ceasefire":** isolated strike days still occurred:
  - Apr 19: an Iranian cargo ship disabled while enforcing the blockade.
  - May 7 (Trump called it a "love tap"): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_May_2026_United_States_strikes_on_Iran
  - May 25, Jun 6, and Jun 27 (possibly with Jun 26 or 28): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire
- **Jul 8 – about Jul 24:** near-daily campaign. The pause began Jul 25.
  - https://www.axios.com/2026/07/26/hormuz-bombing-pause-trump-iran
  - https://time.com/article/2026/08/03/us-iran-war-talks-on-off-fighting-pause-history-timeline/
- **August:** 1 strike day (Aug 30).
- **September:** about 4–5 strike days (Sep 1, maybe Sep 2, Sep 5, Sep 8/9); the tanker strikes may not have been in Iranian waters.

**Share of days with a strike** (the agent's estimates; tanker strikes counted even where location is uncertain)

| Period | Share of days |
|---|---|
| June | about 7–13% |
| July | about 45–50% |
| August | about 3% |
| September | about 13–17% |
| June–September overall | about 16–21% |
| Last 30 days | about 7–10% |
| Sep 10 – Oct 5 (about 26 days) | 0% |

Strikes come in 1–3-day bursts triggered by Iranian attacks on shipping or US forces, plus one sustained campaign of about two weeks in July. Ceasefires and pauses have never fully stopped isolated US strike days.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, at any time between 00:00 UTC on October 15, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on October 16, 2026, United States armed forces carry out at least one new air, missile, drone, or other direct military strike that impacts a target located on Iranian sovereign land territory (including Iranian islands) or in Iran's territorial waters (within 12 nautical miles of its coast), as reported by U.S. Central Command, the U.S. Department of Defense, or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). It resolves NO otherwise. A "strike" means the deliberate delivery of munitions (bombs, missiles, rockets, armed-drone ordnance, or naval/artillery fire) by U.S. forces against a target; interception of incoming Iranian missiles/drones, defensive fire, surveillance flights, seizures/boardings of vessels, and cyber operations do not count.
letra_pequena: Strikes conducted solely by Israel or any other country, without U.S. forces delivering munitions, do not count. Strikes on Iranian-flagged or Iranian-linked vessels located outside Iran's 12-nautical-mile territorial waters (e.g., in the Gulf of Oman or open Persian Gulf) do not count, as the target is not inside Iranian territory. If no credible reporting establishes that such a strike occurred within the window, the question resolves NO.
razonamientos:
(a) As of October 5, the window begins in about 10 days; the outcome will be known after October 16, about 12 days away.

(b) **Status quo: NO.** US strikes inside Iranian territory are paused, and reported planning points toward renewed bombing after the November midterms.

(c) **Reference class:** During the recent lull, there have been no confirmed qualifying strikes in roughly 26 days. Earlier pauses still saw occasional strike days, so the base rate is low but not zero.

(d) **NO scenario:** The US maintains its pre-election restraint through October 16, despite continued maritime harassment.

(e) **YES scenario:** An Iranian attack on US forces or ships prompts a rapid US strike on an Iranian coastal site or island during the two-day window.

(f) **Technicality:** A strike on an Iranian-linked vessel outside Iran’s 12-nautical-mile territorial waters does not count; nor does an Israeli strike without US-delivered munitions.

Probability: 5%

(a) **Time left:** The window closes at 23:59 UTC on October 16, about 11–12 days from October 5. Reporting could take longer.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. The US is in an operational lull, with no recent confirmed strike inside Iranian territory.

(c) **Reference class:** In August and September 2026, there were two clearly identified days with US strikes on Iranian land or islands out of 61 days. That crude rate suggests roughly a 6% chance across two days, though strikes cluster and the recent lull matters.

(d) **NO scenario:** The US maintains its pre-midterm restraint despite maritime harassment and proxy clashes.

(e) **YES scenario:** An Iranian attack on US forces or ships prompts a rapid US retaliatory strike on an Iranian coastal or island target during the window.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A US strike on an Iranian-linked vessel counts only if the target is within Iran’s 12-nautical-mile territorial waters. Israeli-only strikes and US interceptions do not count.

The ongoing war leaves a real risk of retaliation, but the recent pause and reported preference to defer renewed bombing make NO substantially more likely.

Probability: 5%

**(a) Time left:** The window opens in about 10 days (Oct 15, 00:00 UTC) and closes about 12 days from now (Oct 16, 23:59 UTC). The outcome should be known within a day or two after that.

**(b) Status quo:** No strike. There have been no US strikes on Iranian territory since about Sep 10, a run of roughly 26 days. Trump has signalled he expects renewed bombing after the Nov 3 midterms, which implies restraint before then.

**(c) Reference class and base rate:**
- From June to September, strikes fell on about 16–21% of days. They came in clustered bursts of 1–3 days, usually set off by Iranian attacks on US ships or bases.
- Under the current lull regime (Sep 10 onward), the daily rate is close to zero.
- The Polymarket ceasefire ladder moves from 89% for Oct 15 to 73% for Oct 31. That implies about 1–1.5% chance per day of a "break" in mid-to-late October. Its definition of a break is broader and unclear, and Oct 15 is the only bracket with meaningful volume.
- Over a 2-day window, that gives roughly 2–5%.

**(d) No scenario:** The pre-midterm restraint holds. Iran keeps harassing shipping and proxies keep up low-level clashes, but nothing directly hits US forces hard enough to force a response. US action stays limited to the blockade, interceptions, or strikes on vessels outside the 12 nm limit.

**(e) Yes scenario:** Around Oct 13–16, Iran or the IRGC attacks a US warship or base and causes casualties. Within 0–3 days, CENTCOM hits IRGC launchers or boats on Qeshm, Larak or the Bandar Abbas coast, as it did on Aug 30 and Sep 5. Alternatively, the mediation track collapses and Trump moves early.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- Strikes on tankers count only if the tanker is within 12 nm of Iran's coast. Earlier strikes near Kharg and Jask were ambiguous on this point, and a similar case could come down to location.
- Israeli-only strikes do not count.
- The strike must impact the target within the UTC window, so the time-zone boundary matters.

The risk of a tit-for-tat strike is real, but the window is only two days and the current regime is restrained.

Probability: 5%
